observation.visible_scene: A top-down view of a plain white surface on which two hands (the right forearm hairy) manipulate a cluster of glossy black spherical magnets. At the start the hands cradle a single large, roughly pyramidal blob of spheres; by the end the blob has been split into a large cluster resting on the left and a small ring/flower-shaped group of spheres resting on the right, with the hands hovering over them.
visible_changes: Frames 1-11: both hands hold the same large cluster of black spheres, thumbs pressing on the front/top, with only small squeezing/rotating adjustments; the cluster stays as one mass.
Frames 12-18: the right hand grips a smaller subset of spheres and begins pulling it away from the larger mass still held by the left hand; the two groups separate.

Frames 19-30: the right hand now holds the separated subset, which appears as a ring/flower arrangement of about six spheres, and moves it rightward while the left hand keeps the larger cluster on the left.
Frames 31-38: the right hand lowers the ring-shaped group onto the white surface on the right and releases it; the left hand shifts toward the larger left cluster.
Frames 39-41: the small ring of spheres sits on the surface to the right, the large cluster remains to the left, and both hands move away/adjust near them.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the large cluster was assembled before frame 1.
Whether the ring shape was pre-formed or created during the separation (the pulling and the ring are seen together).
What the hands do after frame 41 (rejoining, further splitting, or stopping).
uncertain_details: Exact count of spheres in each group.
Whether any camera movement occurs (background is uniform white, so motion is judged as object/hand movement only).
Precise moment the right hand first made contact with the subset that became the ring.
